stringset_getter_no_dedicated_test.summary: StringSet::contains/iter/len/is_empty/as_set are pure getters wrapping a BTreeSet. There are no unit tests that exercise the getter functions directly with their declared semantics; they are exercised indirectly through ModelCard validation, which only tests the boolean outcome (rejected/accepted), not the precise count, iteration order, or set membership returned. Replacing the getters with constants (false/true/0/1/empty/once) does not change the outer accept/reject decision in any test.
stringset_getter_no_dedicated_test.follow_up: Add unit tests in card.rs that exercise StringSet::contains, ::iter, ::len, ::is_empty, and ::as_set directly with assertions on the exact return value (cardinality, contained elements). Estimated 6-8 short test functions; closes 11 of 20 missed mutants.

boundary_condition_replace_lt_with_le.summary: ModelCard::validate at card.rs:226 rejects only when `expires_at < issued_at` (so exactly-equal `expires_at == issued_at` is currently accepted as a zero-duration card); ModelCard::require_live at card.rs:237 accepts only when `now < expires_at` (so exactly-equal `now == expires_at` is currently rejected as Expired). Replacing `<` with `<=` flips each boundary: line 226 would start rejecting equal timestamps, line 237 would start accepting them. The test suite has no fixture landing exactly on either boundary, so the mutations are silent.
boundary_condition_replace_lt_with_le.follow_up: Add two card.rs unit tests pinning the current accept/reject semantics: (a) ModelCard::validate with expires_at == issued_at MUST currently return Ok(()) (zero-duration card is permitted), so a test asserting Ok(()) catches the `< -> <=` mutation at line 226; (b) ModelCard::require_live with now == expires_at MUST currently return WeightsError::Expired, so a test asserting Expired catches the `< -> <=` mutation at line 237. The polarity matters: pinning these to today's behavior (not the desired strict semantics) is what kills the mutants. Estimated 2 short test functions; closes 2 of 20 missed mutants.

anchor_projection_bytes_constant_returns.summary: anchor_projection_bytes returns Result<Vec<u8>, WeightsError>. Replacing with Ok(vec![]) / Ok(vec![0]) / Ok(vec![1]) is missed because verify_model_card_anchor compares byte slices but the call sites that anchor a card and then verify the returned anchor compute both the produced and expected projection through this same helper, so a constant short-circuit on both sides matches. The lineage_anchor.rs published_card_anchor_verifies_round_trip test only round-trips through the same helper.
anchor_projection_bytes_constant_returns.follow_up: Add a lineage.rs unit test that pins anchor_projection_bytes to a known good fixture (hard-coded golden bytes for a known card+attestation pair) and asserts byte-equality against the helper output. Estimated 1 test function; closes 3 of 20 missed mutants.

sha256_hex_constant_returns.summary: sha256_hex is a private helper around hex::encode(Sha256::digest(_)). Replacing with String::new() or "xyzzy".into() is missed because the helper is called twice on the same input on both sides of the verification (anchor produces, verifier recomputes), so a constant short-circuit on both sides agrees with itself.
sha256_hex_constant_returns.follow_up: Add a lineage.rs unit test that locks sha256_hex against a published RFC 6234 / NIST FIPS 180-4 vector (e.g. SHA-256("abc") = ba7816bf...). Estimated 1 test function; closes 2 of 20 missed mutants.

verify_model_card_anchor_negation_delete.summary: verify_model_card_anchor at line 288 has a `!` that is being deleted by the mutator. The deletion does not flip a tested branch in any test fixture, suggesting the negated condition either always evaluates the same way under tested fixtures or the negation is on a defensive check (e.g. a fast-path return) that never triggers in tests.
verify_model_card_anchor_negation_delete.follow_up: Read lineage.rs:288 in detail to identify the exact condition and add a test fixture that exercises both branches. Estimated 1 test function; closes 1 of 20 missed mutants.

missed_mutant_categories.summary_estimate: All 20 missed mutants are addressable by adding ~10-12 short, focused unit tests to card.rs (StringSet getters, boundary conditions) and lineage.rs (anchor_projection_bytes / sha256_hex golden fixtures, verify_model_card_anchor negation branch). The test additions are deferred to a follow-up PR; this PR's scope is the BASELINE measurement only. Closing the gap would push the kill rate from 68.3% toward 100% on this surface.
